english: The tangent to the curve $y=\dfrac{2}{1+x^{2}}$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$, at the point where $x=1$ touches the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{3}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$, $0<b<\sqrt3$, at the point $(\alpha,\beta)$. Then the value of $\beta$ is ______.
hindi: वक्र $y=\dfrac{2}{1+x^{2}}$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$, के उस बिन्दु पर, जहाँ $x=1$ है, खींची गई स्पर्श रेखा दीर्घवृत्त $\dfrac{x^{2}}{3}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$, $0<b<\sqrt3$, को बिन्दु $(\alpha,\beta)$ पर स्पर्श करती है। तब $\beta$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: At $x=1$: $y=\dfrac{2}{2}=1$. $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{4x}{(1+x^{2})^{2}}$, so the slope at $x=1$ is $-\dfrac{4}{4}=-1$.

The point of contact of the tangent $y=mx+c$ is $\left(-\dfrac{a^{2}m}{c},\dfrac{b^{2}}{c}\right)=\left(\dfrac{3}{2},\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$. Check: it is on $x+y=2$ and $\dfrac{9/4}{3}+\dfrac14=\dfrac34+\dfrac14=1$.
originality_note: New: one line is the tangent to a non-conic curve at a given point and must also touch an ellipse with unknown minor axis; the contact point follows from the tangency condition (way 5). Closest known: condition for y = mx + c to touch an ellipse; common tangents of two conics. Different because: the line comes from calculus on y = 2/(1 + x^2), and the unknown b is fixed by the tangency condition before the contact point is read.
stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, point and curve introduced, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; answer matches the plan. Checked that b^2 = 1 lies in the stated range, that the contact point is on both line and ellipse, and that the answer is exact. Changed: No change.
key_step: Tangent y = 2 - x from the derivative, then c^2 = a^2 m^2 + b^2 gives b^2 = 1 and the contact point (3/2, 1/2).
justification: Routine three-step chain across two chapters (derivative, tangency condition, contact point); nothing unfamiliar. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q2 (L2), tangent slopes on several curves.
blueprint_concepts: Equation of a tangent to a curve

concept_use.Tangent and normal for Ellipse: The tangency condition c^2 = a^2 m^2 + b^2 fixes b^2 = 1, and the contact point (-a^2 m/c, b^2/c) of a tangent to the ellipse gives beta = 1/2.
concept_use.Equation of a tangent to a curve: The tangent to y = 2/(1 + x^2) at x = 1 is found from dy/dx = -4x/(1 + x^2)^2: y = -x + 2.
